messages:
maya: Quick follow-up on the quota-sharding idea from last week's RFC — I sketched two concrete implementations and want to surface tradeoffs before we lock one in.

raj: awesome, lay it out. will help with the Dedicated tenant problems.

maya: option A = deterministic shard key (tenant_id % num_shards) with local buckets per shard. Simple, predictable routing, cheap counters. Downsides: hot tenants cause imbalanced load and need a heavy rebalancer to move state.

linus: +1 on simplicity. but how do we handle bursty tenants without global coordination? we could add local burst buffers and probabilistic reject when over local cap.

maya: agreed. local burst helps but then fairness across tenants suffers. Option B = lease-based admission: short-lived token leases allocated from a central allocator; shards request leases as needed. That gives global fairness but adds allocator latency and one more availability surface.

carla: lease allocator seems heavy. what's the failure mode? allocator down => all admission stops?

maya: we propose fallback: when allocator unreachable, shards fallback to cached per-tenant soft-quotas with conservative limits and emit alerts. degraded mode but not hard outage.

olivia: what about counting accuracy? we need token accounting for both streaming and non-streaming requests. Streaming makes it tricky to know total tokens pre-admit.

raj: for streaming we can admit based on next-K tokens estimate and then reconcile with refunds/adjustments. also use bounded overcommit windows. example: admit up to min(estimate, lease_remaining + slack).

linus: sounds fine but requires good telemetry to avoid abuse. we should tie this to our abuse score service so we can throttle or penalize leaky/high-error tenants quickly.

maya: yes — integrate with abuse-service: tenants get dynamic penalty_factor that scales their effective quota. penalty_factor decays over time. We can expose policy: if abuse_score > 0.7 => penalty_factor = 0.5 (halves throughput).

carla: question on rebalancer: if we migrate tenant state across shards, do we move lease ownership too? migration must be atomic-ish to avoid double-spend.

maya: propose migrate steps: 1) mark tenant read-only on source shard, 2) allocate target shard lease, 3) move counters (snapshot + deltas), 4) flip routing. aim for idempotent ops with short overlap TTL.

olivia: sounds operationally complex. can we avoid live migration by making shard count elastic and always route via consistent hash + virtual nodes? then we just add/remove nodes without moving tenant data manually.

raj: consistent hashing helps, but hot-splitting still needs moving a hot-tenant to a new virtual node. also consistent hashing doesn't solve cross-shard fairness if two heavy tenants map to same physical host.

linus: telemetry/prio: we need per-tenant token histograms, short-window qps, and a tail-latency signal so autoscaling / rebalancer has good inputs. this is critical for both options.

maya: agree. Operational concerns: metrics we need out of the gate: per-shard tokens/s, per-tenant recent_tokens (1s/1m/1h), lease_alloc_failures, migration_failures, and penalty_effectiveness.

carla: rollout plan? I'd prefer start with Option A + soft global monitor that suggests rebalances. low blast radius, can iterate.

maya: proposal: implement Option A with: (a) per-shard counters + local burst buffer, (b) global balancer service that only recommends rebalancing (manual/automated off-by-default), (c) abuse-service integration to apply penalty_factor, (d) doc + small eval suite with synthetic hot-tenant tests.

olivia: agree. add a canary that routes 5% traffic through lease-allocator path to validate option B feasibility.

raj: one more: store counters in memory with periodic checkpoint to Redis for fast restart. design must ensure counter monotonicity across restarts.

maya: noted. checkpoint scheme: append-only delta logs per tenant every 10s, snapshot every 5m. on restart replay deltas to rebuild.

linus: small config snippet for the permissive fallback we discussed:
```yaml
admission:
  mode: local-first
  local_burst_tokens: 1000
  soft_global_threshold_pct: 70
  fallback_policy:
    allocator_unavailable: conservative
```

sre-bot: deploy-checklist created: "quota-shard-A-rollout" with steps: feature-flag gating, canary, smoke tests, monitoring alerts.

maya: thanks all — i'll open a follow-up PR with the design doc + the eval harness. please drop comments on the PR for any missed edge cases. :thumbsup:
